rot.clubTraps.ideia.ex1.e1: Attack: with Black, in the Stafford Defence. In the previous lesson, in this opening, White developed the bishop on f1 and took care of the kingside.
rot.clubTraps.ideia.ex1.e2: A gambit is giving up material in the opening, usually a pawn, to gain development time or an attack. Black gave up the pawn on e5 and already has the bishop and the knight aimed at the white king.
rot.clubTraps.ideia.ex1.e3: Here White took the bishop from c1 to g5. It attacks your knight on f6, which is pinned to the queen on d8.
rot.clubTraps.ideia.ex1.p: Use Black's development. Find the best move.
rot.clubTraps.ideia.ex1.certo: The knight captures the pawn on e4 and leaves the queen attacked on purpose. If the bishop captures the queen, the bishop on c5 and the knight give mate.
rot.clubTraps.ideia.ex1.revela: The best move was the knight capturing the pawn on e4 and leaving the queen attacked on purpose: if the bishop captures the queen, Black gives mate.
rot.clubTraps.ideia.ex1.alt.c5f2.1: The bishop captures the pawn on f2 with check, and this move also wins: after the king captures the bishop, the knight captures on e4 with check, and the queen on d1 or the bishop on g5 is left undefended.
rot.clubTraps.ideia.ex1.alt.c5f2.2: Back to the position: now see the strongest move, the knight to e4, which sets the trap.
rot.clubTraps.ideia.ex1.err.d8d4.1: The queen goes to d4 and attacks the pawns on f2 and b2.
rot.clubTraps.ideia.ex1.err.d8d4.2: With this move White has a resource: the bishop retreats to h4 and defends the pawn on f2. Black only wins back a pawn, and the position is balanced.
rot.clubTraps.ideia.ex1.err.d8d4.3: Back to the position: the bishop on g5 attacks your knight and your queen. Look for the move that turns that attack into a trap.
rot.clubTraps.ideia.ex1.err.h7h6.1: The h7 pawn advances and attacks the bishop on g5.
rot.clubTraps.ideia.ex1.err.h7h6.2: With this move White has a resource: the bishop goes to e3 and offers an exchange for the bishop on c5, which was aiming at f2. Without that bishop, Black's attack loses strength.
rot.clubTraps.ideia.ex1.err.h7h6.3: Back to the position: the bishop on g5 attacks your knight and your queen. Look for the move that turns that attack into a trap.
rot.clubTraps.ideia.ex1.err.e8g8.1: Black castles and puts the king in safety.
rot.clubTraps.ideia.ex1.err.e8g8.2: With this move White has a resource: the knight goes to d2 and defends the pawn on e4. Black is a pawn down and has no attack.
rot.clubTraps.ideia.ex1.err.e8g8.3: Back to the position: the bishop on g5 attacks your knight and your queen. Look for the move that turns that attack into a trap.
rot.clubTraps.ideia.ex1.fora: That move gives White time to develop and defend the pawn on e4. Look for a move that turns the bishop on g5 against White.
rot.clubTraps.ideia.ex1.volta: Try again: look for the trap.
rot.clubTraps.ideia.ex1.l0: Now White moves. The black queen is still attacked by the bishop on g5, and capturing it looks easy.
rot.clubTraps.ideia.ex1.l1: The white bishop captures the queen: it is the move that seems to win the most material.
rot.clubTraps.ideia.ex1.l2: The bishop captures on f2 with check: early in the game, only the king defends that pawn. The knight on e4 supports the bishop, and the white king only has the e2 square.
rot.clubTraps.ideia.ex1.l3: The king goes to e2, the only square.
rot.clubTraps.ideia.ex1.l4: The bishop on c8 goes to g4 and gives mate. The white and the black pieces close every square around the king.
rot.clubTraps.ideia.ex1.l5: White captured the queen and had no time left to defend the king. Facing an offer like this, check what the opponent threatens before capturing.
rot.clubTraps.ideia.ex2.e1: Defence: now with White, in the Englund Gambit. Black gave up the pawn on e5 on the very first move to attack early with the queen.
rot.clubTraps.ideia.ex2.e2: The black queen captured the pawn on b2 and attacks the rook on a1. Facing a gambit, the calm reply develops a piece and defends what is attacked.
rot.clubTraps.ideia.ex2.p: The rook on a1 is attacked. Find the best move.
rot.clubTraps.ideia.ex2.certo: The knight goes to c3 and develops. With the knight off b1, the queen on d1 now defends the rook on a1.
rot.clubTraps.ideia.ex2.revela: The best move was the knight to c3: it develops, and the queen on d1 now defends the rook on a1.
rot.clubTraps.ideia.ex2.err.d2c3.1: The bishop goes to c3, attacks the queen and blocks her path to the rook on a1.
rot.clubTraps.ideia.ex2.err.d2c3.2: With this move Black has a resource: the bishop goes to b4 and pins the bishop on c3 to the king. It cannot capture the queen, and the rook on a1 is still attacked.
rot.clubTraps.ideia.ex2.err.d2c3.3: Back to the position: look for a move that develops a new piece and defends the rook on a1.
rot.clubTraps.ideia.ex2.fora: That move does not deal with the threat: the black queen stays active and Black wins back the material. Look for a move that develops a piece and defends the rook on a1.
rot.clubTraps.ideia.ex2.l0: Now Black moves. The queen on b2 is still in White's camp and looks for another target.
rot.clubTraps.ideia.ex2.l1: The black bishop goes to b4 and attacks the knight on c3 a second time, together with the queen. The bishop on d2 defends it.
rot.clubTraps.ideia.ex2.l2: The rook goes to b1, escapes and attacks the queen.
rot.clubTraps.ideia.ex2.l3: The queen retreats to a3, far from the other black pieces.
rot.clubTraps.ideia.ex2.l4: Material is level, but White has four pieces in play, and the black queen has spent time. The calm reply gave back the pawn and kept the lead in development.
rot.clubTraps.demos.shilling.1: Attack: now with Black, in the Blackburne Shilling Gambit. The black knight went to d4 and left the pawn on e5, and the white knight has just captured it.
rot.clubTraps.demos.shilling.l.1: The queen goes to g5 and attacks the knight on e5 and the pawn on g2 at the same time.
rot.clubTraps.demos.shilling.l.2: The knight captures the pawn on f7 and attacks the rook on h8: White tries to win even more material and forgets the pawn on g2.
rot.clubTraps.demos.shilling.l.3: The queen captures the pawn on g2 and attacks the rook on h1.
rot.clubTraps.demos.shilling.l.4: The rook escapes to f1, the most natural move to save it.
rot.clubTraps.demos.shilling.l.5: The queen captures the pawn on e4 with check.
rot.clubTraps.demos.shilling.l.6: The bishop goes back to e2 and blocks the check. Now it is pinned by the queen to the king.
rot.clubTraps.demos.shilling.l.7: The knight goes to f3 and gives mate. The pinned bishop cannot capture it, and the king is surrounded by its own pieces: it is a smothered mate.
rot.clubTraps.demos.shilling.l.8: Back to the position: White fell into the trap by capturing too much. One move earlier, the calm reply was the knight on f3 capturing the knight on d4.
rot.clubTraps.demos.legal.1: Attack: with White, in a game played on Lichess. The black bishop has just captured the queen on d1, which White gave up on purpose. It is Légal's trap, from the 18th century.
rot.clubTraps.demos.legal.l.1: The bishop captures the pawn on f7 with check. The knight on e5 defends it, and the black king only has the e7 square.
rot.clubTraps.demos.legal.l.2: The king goes to e7, the only square.
rot.clubTraps.demos.legal.l.3: The knight on c3 goes to d5 and gives mate. The black pieces block their own king's squares, and the knights and the bishop cover the rest.
rot.clubTraps.demos.legal.l.4: A queen down, White gave mate in two moves. The black bishop that captured the queen was far from its own king.
rot.clubTraps.demos.excecao.1: Attack: with White, in the Fried Liver Attack. The knight on g5 and the bishop on c4 aim at the pawn on f7, which only the king defends.
rot.clubTraps.demos.excecao.l.1: The knight captures the pawn on f7 and attacks the queen and the rook. White gives up the knight to drag the king out.
rot.clubTraps.demos.excecao.l.2: The king captures the knight: Black accepts the extra piece.
rot.clubTraps.demos.excecao.l.3: The queen gives check and attacks the knight on d5, together with the bishop on c4.
rot.clubTraps.demos.excecao.l.4: The king goes to e6 and defends the knight on d5.
rot.clubTraps.demos.excecao.l.5: The knight on b1 develops and attacks the knight on d5 a third time.
rot.clubTraps.demos.excecao.l.6: The knight on c6 goes to b4 and defends d5 once more. White has an attack, but the piece given up does not come back by force, and their advantage is small.
rot.clubTraps.demos.excecao.l.7: Back to the position: here capturing on f7 does not decide, and a calm move, such as pushing the d2 pawn two squares, also gives an advantage. Giving up material calls for calculation: the position decides.
rot.clubTraps.pratica.valeAqui.enunciado: Now with Black, in the Giuoco Piano. The pawn on f2 has only the king as a defender, and your bishop on c5 aims at that square. Is it worth capturing on f2 now? Play as Black and find the best move.
rot.clubTraps.pratica.valeAqui.fim: You kept developing without giving up material. Here no other black piece supports the bishop on f2, and capturing would only have given White an extra piece.
rot.clubTraps.pratica.valeAqui.err.c5f2: The bishop captures on f2 with check, but the king takes it, and no black piece carries on the attack. Black is left with a pawn for a piece. Develop instead of capturing.
rot.clubTraps.pratica.ataque.enunciado: Now with White, in a game played on Lichess. The h-file is open, but your bishop on h5 stands between the rook on h1 and the black rook on h8. Play as White and find the best move.
rot.clubTraps.pratica.ataque.fim: The bishop left the h-file with check on f7: it is a discovered attack, and the check gave Black no time. The rook captured the rook on h8, and you won a rook for a bishop.
rot.clubTraps.pratica.ataque.err.c1e3: The bishop develops, but it leaves the pawn on b2 undefended: the queen on b6 captures it and attacks the rook on a1. Look for a way to use the h-file without giving Black time.
rot.clubTraps.pratica.ataque.err.g2g4: The pawn attacks the bishop on f5, but Black has time to look after the rook on h8. Look for a way to use the h-file without giving Black time.
rot.clubTraps.pratica.gula.enunciado: Now with White, in a game played on Lichess. The black knight captured your pawn on e4 and left the queen on d8 attacked by the bishop on g5. Play as White and find the best move.
rot.clubTraps.pratica.gula.fim: You did not fall into the trap. Capturing the queen left the pawn on f2 undefended: the bishop on c5 gave check on f2, and the knight on c6 gave mate on d4.
rot.clubTraps.pratica.gula.err.g5d8: The bishop captures the queen, but the bishop on c5 captures on f2 with check, the king only has e2, and the knight on c6 goes to d4 and gives mate. Before capturing, see what Black threatens.
rot.clubTraps.pratica.gula.err.d3e4: The pawn recaptures on e4, but the queen on d8 captures your bishop on g5, which was left undefended, and Black is a piece up. Before capturing, see what Black threatens.
